fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 has no polynomial-time construction rule: its SAT search quantifies over every perfect matching, thereby using the NP-hard witness set to construct the lift. The sheet routing, target, and resulting binary matrix are also unspecified, while tests at L=3,5 cannot establish the claimed asymptotic amplification.

Proposal 2 cannot compare overlapping scopes using full-scope checksums without a completeness failure: dependence on private variables makes equal overlaps produce unequal checksums. Projecting away private variables factors communication through a proper overlap signature and re-enters O2/O3, including the certified holonomy pseudoassignments.

Proposal 3 does not specify the subspace-design objective, selected maps, block count, or deterministic selection algorithm. For a pure witness W=xx^T, the cross blocks contain t(R_sx)^T and (R_sx)t^T, so sparse YES cost is unproved and may be densified exactly as in the failed F8 condenser.

Proposal 4 lacks a completeness-preserving jet lift of an unknown nearest Reed–Solomon polynomial. Ordinary value agreement gives only a simple root of the discrepancy, not agreement of higher derivatives, so multiplicity coordinates can inflate YES distance; the zero-multiplicity bound does not multiply each ordinary disagreement by s.

Proposal 5 is defeated by linear affine closure unless it supplies separate nonlinearly protected legal sectors. Three cheap fillings of the same binary target XOR to another target-fiber filling of at most three times their total support, and existing illegal odd covers already occur in affine spans of legal matchings.

Proposal 6 has an explicit layer-constant obstruction: repeat the cheapest illegal exact cover in every layer and every expander-difference row vanishes, just as for a matching. Both YES and NO norms then scale by the layer count, retaining only the additive q versus q+2 defect; bounded coefficient search cannot repair this parameter failure.

Proposal 7 starts from a false structural premise: partial 3DM packings are not the independent sets of one linear matroid, since 3-set packing violates matroid exchange. Even in applicable matroids, representative-family size is exponential at rank Θ(q), and identifying terminal states that cannot extend to a matching embeds the source NP-hard decision.
evidence: The exchange-quotient verifier found 32 instances where an illegal odd cover lies in the affine span of perfect matchings. This directly obstructs Proposal 5 and any linear protected-class mechanism that makes all legal fillings cheap.
The twisted-holonomy and Petersen witnesses certify failures of proper connected scopes and fixed-level overlap systems. Proposal 2 provides no global interface escaping those hypotheses.

The frozen two-sided F8 condenser had worst YES 31 versus best NO 6 despite avoiding pointed kernels. This is finite adverse evidence, not a universal theorem, but Proposal 3 supplies no new rank-to-support lemma addressing the observed failure.

Direct integer exact cover rigorously gives only q versus q+2, while variable projection tables gave 12 versus 14. Proposal 6's layer-constant witness preserves that additive regime rather than amplifying it.

No supplied verifier implements any of the seven proposed matrices or establishes their claimed separation. Their suggested finite searches either depend on witness enumeration, omit a complete matrix and target, or test only constants unrelated to the missing asymptotic mechanism.
next_experiment: None for the proposals as written. Reopen only after a mutation supplies an explicit polynomial-time matrix and target without enumerating matchings; the closest viable mutation is Proposal 3 with fully frozen binary maps and a proof of witness-independent YES support, followed by exhaustive all-mixed-word, affine-closure, all-eight, and holonomy testing.
